page: UpCloud GPU-96xCPU-960GB-4xB200 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 96 shared vCPUs and 960.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory allocation of 10.0 GB per core. The server does not include local storage, meaning storage resources must be attached externally. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The defining characteristic of this server is its integrated GPU acceleration, featuring four NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs. These GPUs provide a combined total of 768 GB of VRAM. This hardware profile is designed for heavy parallel processing tasks, particularly those requiring massive graphics memory capacity and high-density compute resources.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a high-end hardware class with extreme resource density, balancing a large memory footprint with top-tier accelerator hardware. The shared CPU allocation suggests that while GPU-bound tasks will run at maximum hardware capacity, CPU-bound tasks may experience resource sharing. This configuration is suited for large-scale machine learning model training, deep learning inference, data science pipelines, and complex parallel computing workloads.
